title: Ram Murat v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal and Jayant Banerji, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.10 representation.
headnote: A consumer writ against the State and the distribution licensee is not maintainable where clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords an alternative statutory remedy by representation. Non-appearance of the petitioner does not prevent dismissal on that ground when departmental counsel so submits.
facts: Ram Murat filed Writ-C No. 22547 of 2020 in the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad against the State of Uttar Pradesh and two others, seeking relief on electricity grievances. The petition was listed before a Division Bench on 15 December 2020. When the matter was called, none appeared for the petitioner. Counsel for the respondent-Department was present and submitted that the grievances could be addressed if a representation were made under clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: A writ raising consumer electricity grievances is dismissed where clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies an alternative statutory remedy by representation; the court will not entertain the petition on that ground.

principle_tags.application: Writ dismissed solely because clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was treated as an available alternative statutory remedy for the petitioner's grievances.

not_decided.point: merits of the petitioner's electricity grievances
not_decided.note: The court did not examine the underlying supply dispute; dismissal rested only on the alternative clause 6.10 remedy.
